notes: BOOT button shares GPIO35 with ETH RMII TXD1; it cannot be used as a runtime input while Ethernet is enabled (BSP_CAPS_BUTTONS=0).

GT911 touch, ES8311 audio codec, and SC2336/OV5647 SCCB all share one I2C0 bus (SDA=GPIO7, SCL=GPIO8). These pins are GPIOMatrix-routable, so they are not flagged reserved, but the board hard-wires all three devices here.

MIPI CSI and MIPI DSI lanes use dedicated pads in the VDD_MIPI_DPHY domain and are NOT routable through GPIOMatrix; they are therefore omitted from peripherals (which only stores GPIO-routable defaults). Only the DSI reset (GPIO27) and backlight PWM (GPIO26) are GPIO-level and listed under lcd_mipi0.

GPIO26 (LCD backlight PWM via LEDC5, J1.31) and GPIO27 (LCD reset, J6 RST_LCD) are the recommended defaults for the optional 7-inch LCD, set via DuPont jumpers to the LCD adapter's J6 header. They are NOT flagged reserved because the LCD is an optional accessory and users without it may reuse these GPIOs (the Pin Planner still applies the boardRule warning only for genuinely hardwired pins).

NS4150B audio PA enable (GPIO53, BSP_POWER_AMP_IO) is reserved=true: it is a hardwired onboard control line (not broken out on J1) and re-assigning GPIO53 to another peripheral disables speaker output.

microSD slot is wired in 4-bit SDMMC mode: CLK=GPIO43, CMD=GPIO44, D0-D3=GPIO39-42. The SD-SPI fallback shares the same pins. These are onboard hardware but left reserved=false (per DevKitC convention) so users can intentionally re-route them; they are listed in onboardPins, so taking them over for another peripheral raises a board-level warning instead of a hard block.
Ethernet RMII (IP101 PHY) uses ESP-IDF ESP32-P4 software defaults: MDC=31, MDIO=52, REF_CLK in=50, TX_EN=49, TXD0=34, TXD1=35, CRS_DV=28, RXD0=29, RXD1=30, PHY reset=51.

onboardPins lists GPIOs physically wired to an on-board device (shared I2C0 bus, ES8311 audio, microSD SDMMC, IP101 Ethernet RMII, UART0 bridge). Unlike reservedGpios they remain usable: assigning the matching board default (uart0 on 37/38, i2s0 on 9-13, i2c0 on 7/8) is not reported, while taking the pin over for a different owner produces a board-level warning.
